Reference Text: Although an Leshy, Pebble Spring became immediately fascinated by the mortal settlements when they set foot in a city. They loves the nicely paved ground, the intricate bridges, and the most of all, they loved houses. The nicely layed out stone walls forming shelters from the weathers yet connect the earth with the stories from every family. They decided to learn the craft of housebuilding with the help of a touch of arcane magic from their self-made staff.

message.content: Pebble Spring arrived at the city gates on a bright autumn morning, their mossy cloak fluttering in the crisp wind. The stone archway above the gate was carved with intricate patterns of ivy and small blossoms. They stepped forward, their hooves clicking rhythmically against the cobblestones. A guard at the gate looked up with surprise, having never seen a Leshy so close before. "Welcome to Thornhaven," the guard said, his voice warm and welcoming. Pebble Spring nodded politely, their staff tapping the ground in a gentle salute. The streets beyond the gate were bustling with merchants, children, and curious onlookers. They wandered past the bakeries, where the smell of fresh bread wafted through the narrow lanes. Each shop displayed its wares with great pride, from bolts of silk to jars of pickled plums. Pebble Spring paused at a bookshop, their eyes widening at the towering shelves of leather-bound volumes. The owner, a tiny old woman with spectacles perched on her nose, invited them inside. They spent the entire afternoon reading about construction techniques from distant lands. By evening, they had filled three notebooks with sketches and measurements. The old woman laughed kindly and offered them a pot of warm tea as a reward. Pebble Spring accepted graciously, sipping it while watching the sunset paint the sky in hues of gold. The next morning, they visited the city's famous quarry to observe how stone was cut and shaped. The masons there were impressive, their hammers ringing in a steady, musical rhythm. One young mason, noticing the Leshy's fascinated stare, invited them to try swinging a chisel. The first strike was clumsy, sending a chunk of rock flying toward a nearby barrel. Pebble Spring apologized profusely, their leafy hair rustling with embarrassment. The mason merely grinned and handed them a smaller tool, explaining the proper angle. With their natural connection to the earth, Pebble Spring quickly found a rhythm in the work. By the end of the week, their small practice structure stood as a testament to their growing skill. The following several days brought a long and tedious series of unexpected challenges, from learning to mix mortar properly to understanding how to lay courses without leaving any gaps, and though their progress was spotty at times, the encouragement of their new friends kept their spirits bright.
